Kuniv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery was marked as a Jewish burial ground on an 1880s Russian map, and its oldest surviving gravestone dates to the second half of the 19th century. Kuniv's Jewish population tripled between 1847 and 1897, reaching a majority of 56.5 percent, with residents active in crafts and trade. On August 4, 1941, 159 Jews from Kuniv and neighboring Malaya Radogoshchi were shot near this cemetery, and hundreds of Jewish artisans — initially spared for their labor — were murdered the following June.
